text: While I await those lab results, has the rash appeared in a specific pattern, such as a "halo" around each bump, or does it have a central crater? Additionally, have you noticed any joint pain, fever, or recent sun exposure?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lupus Pernio (cutaneous lupus erythematosus). The chronic, pruritic nature of the rash on the upper extremities in a young female, combined with the pending ANA and ESR results, strongly suggests an autoimmune etiology rather than an infectious or drug-induced cause. Have you noticed any photosensitivity or joint stiffness? REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_scan_upper_extremities
